```{r setup, include=FALSE}

```

H1: Respondents who spent most of their childhood in France rate infidelity as less morally wrong than respondents raised elsewhere.

H2: Respondents who spend more time per day on their appearance are more jealous about their partner's sexual infidelity.

## Variables

- **H1, independent variable:** `Country_raised` (country where the respondent spent most of childhood)
- **H1, dependent variables:** `infmoral_sex` and `infmoral_emo` (1 = Not at all morally wrong, 7 = Extremely morally wrong)
- **H2, independent variable:** sum of the eight `Time_A_` items (minutes per day, each 0 to 360)
- **H2, dependent variable:** `jealsex` (1 = Not at all jealous, 7 = Extremely jealous)

## 1. Load the package and data

```{r load, message=FALSE}
#load the codebook package
library(codebook)

#load data/raw/data_doctored.csv
raw<-read.csv("../Data/Raw Data/data_doctored.csv")

#check row and column counts, and inspect the first few rows
dim(raw)
str(raw)


#make data with ID, country raised, both infidelity items, the eight appearance time items, and jealsex; keep raw unchanged
timeVars <- c("Time_A_makeup_1", "Time_A_hyg_1", "Time_A_cosm_1", "Time_A_exercise_1",
              "Time_A_hair_1", "Time_A_dress_1", "Time_A_diet_1", "Time_A_other_1")

data <- raw[, c("ResponseId", "Country_raised", "infmoral_sex", "infmoral_emo",
                timeVars, "jealsex")]

dim(data)
str(data)








```


## 2. Check participant IDs

```{r participant_ids}

#count na
sum(is.na(data$ResponseId))

#count blank
sum(data$ResponseId=="",na.rm=TRUE)

#count duplicates
sum(duplicated(data$ResponseId))

#inspect records with missing or blank IDs
missingID<- which(is.na(data$ResponseId))
print(data[missingID,])

#remove the known empty record with no ID, then check the row count
data<-data[!is.na(data$ResponseId),]
dim(data)

```


## 3. Recode country raised

```{r sex_at_birth}
# codebook: Country_raised is country-name text; France is listed as "France"

#check how many people were raised in France
sum(data$Country_raised=="France", na.rm=TRUE)

#turn Country_raised into a factor with labels Elsewhere and France
data$raisedFrance<- ifelse(data$Country_raised=="France", 1, 0)
data$raisedFrance<- factor(data$raisedFrance,
                           levels=c(0,1),
                           labels=c("Elsewhere","France"))
table(data$raisedFrance, useNA="ifany")

```


## 4. Validate infidelity morality items

```{r infidelity_items}
#group both infidelity morality variables
infVars<- c("infmoral_sex","infmoral_emo")

#see summary of variables
summary(data[,infVars])
#count NAs
colSums(is.na(data[,infVars]))

#inspect the response frequencies for each item
for(i in infVars){
  print(i)
  print(table(data[,i],useNA="ifany"))
}

#replace any codes outside 1-7 with NA
#codebook: 1 = Not at all morally wrong, 7 = Extremely morally wrong
for (i in infVars){
  data[,i]<- ifelse(data[,i] %in% 1:7, data[,i], NA)
}


#make h1Data with ID, raisedFrance, infmoral_sex, and infmoral_emo
#keep participants with a known country group and at least one valid rating
h1Data <- data[!is.na(data$raisedFrance) &
                 (!is.na(data$infmoral_sex) | !is.na(data$infmoral_emo)),
               c("ResponseId","raisedFrance","infmoral_sex","infmoral_emo")]

dim(h1Data)
head(h1Data)


```


## 5. Check appearance time and jealousy items
```{r appearance_items}
#define the items to check; the 8 time items are minutes per day
#codebook: each time item is 0-360; 360 means 6 hours or more

#check the summaries and missing responses
summary(data[,timeVars])
colSums(is.na(data[,timeVars]))

#replace any values outside 0-360 with NA
for (i in timeVars){
  data[,i]<- ifelse(data[,i] %in% 0:360, data[,i], NA)
}
colSums(is.na(data[,timeVars]))

#jealsex uses response codes 1-7
#jealsex: 1=Not at all jealous, 7=Extremely jealous
likert7 <- c("jealsex")

#check the summary and missing responses
summary(data$jealsex)
sum(is.na(data$jealsex))

#inspect the response frequencies for each item
for(i in likert7){
  print(i)
  print(table(data[,i],useNA="ifany"))
}

#replace any codes outside 1-7 with NA
for (i in likert7){
  data[,i]<- ifelse(data[,i] %in% 1:7, data[,i], NA)
}
sum(is.na(data$jealsex))

```

## 6. Calculate appearance time

```{r appearance_composite}

#group the appearance time variables (the eight Time_A_ items)
#these are minutes per day

#calculate appearance time as the sum of all eight items
#Put the total NA if any item is missing
data$appearTime<- rowSums(data[,timeVars],na.rm=FALSE)

#check the score
summary(data$appearTime)
sum(!is.na(data$appearTime))

###JK: Your eight-item sum and complete-response rule are clear; please also inspect totals above 24 hours. ###
# In the final H2 table, 500 participants have appearance-time totals above 1,440 minutes, with a maximum of 2,880.
# You can inspect them and explain how you will interpret or handle them.
# After creating h2Data below, you can inspect these cases with:
# sum(h2Data$appearTime > 1440)
# range(h2Data$appearTime)
# head(h2Data[h2Data$appearTime > 1440, ])
###  End of comment ###

#make h2Data with ID, appearTime, and jealsex
#keep participants with both appearTime and jealsex present
h2Data <- data[!is.na(data$appearTime) & !is.na(data$jealsex),
               c("ResponseId","appearTime","jealsex")]

dim(h2Data)
summary(h2Data)

```

## 7. Check the final tables

```{r final_tables}
#check rows, columns, types, and missing values in h1Data
#one row per participant, one column per variable
dim(h1Data)
str(h1Data)
head(h1Data)
colSums(is.na(h1Data))
table(h1Data$raisedFrance,useNA="ifany")
range(h1Data$infmoral_sex,na.rm=TRUE)
range(h1Data$infmoral_emo,na.rm=TRUE)
sum(duplicated(h1Data$ResponseId))

#repeat the checks for h2Data; jealsex should be within 1-7 and appearTime within 0-2880
dim(h2Data)
str(h2Data)
head(h2Data)
colSums(is.na(h2Data))
range(h2Data$appearTime)
range(h2Data$jealsex)
sum(duplicated(h2Data$ResponseId))
```

## 8. Add labels and generate codebooks

The descriptions come from the original codebook and our scoring decisions.
`compact_codebook()` adds summaries from the actual data. Knit the Rmd to
display the formatted codebooks.

```{r variable_labels}
#add a description to each h1Data column, in column order
#include the source codes, meaning, and units
var_label(h1Data) <- c("Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
                       "Country where the respondent spent most of childhood: France or Elsewhere, recoded from the text variable Country_raised; blank country excluded",
                       "How morally wrong sexual infidelity is (infmoral_sex); 1=Not at all morally wrong, 4=Moderately morally wrong, 7=Extremely morally wrong",
                       "How morally wrong emotional infidelity is (infmoral_emo); 1=Not at all morally wrong, 4=Moderately morally wrong, 7=Extremely morally wrong"
)

#add a description to each h2Data column, in column order
#include response anchors and the commitment scoring rule
var_label(h2Data) <- c("Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
                       "Daily time spent enhancing appearance, in minutes: sum of the eight Time_A_ items, each 0-360 where 360 means 6 hours or more; NA if any of the eight is missing",
                       "Jealousy about a partner's purely sexual infidelity (jealsex); 1=Not at all jealous, 4=Moderately jealous, 7=Extremely jealous"
)

```

H1 includes participants with an ID, a known country group (France or Elsewhere), and at least one valid infidelity rating from 1 to 7. Factor level numbers in the generated table are internal R positions, not the original survey codes.

```{r h1_codebook}
#generate the h1Data codebook
compact_codebook(h1Data)

```

H2 includes participants with an ID, valid answers on all eight time items, and a valid jealsex response from 1 to 7.

```{r h2_codebook}
#generate the h2Data codebook
compact_codebook(h2Data)

```

## 9. Save the final tables

```{r save}
#create data/processed_data if needed
dir.create("../Data/processed_data",recursive=T,showWarnings=F)

#save h1Data and h2Data without an extra row-number column
write.csv(h1Data,"../Data/processed_data/project_h1.csv",row.names=F)
write.csv(h2Data,"../Data/processed_data/project_h2.csv",row.names=F)

#read the files back and confirm their dimensions
h1Saved <- read.csv("../Data/processed_data/project_h1.csv")
h2Saved <- read.csv("../Data/processed_data/project_h2.csv")
dim(h1Saved)
dim(h2Saved)

```
